Then specialize Ω to the Library of Babel word space Fin L → Fin b, proving that when b ≥ 2 the uniform Library entropy is exactly L in base b. Drop the overextended claims about arbitrary distributions, min-entropy at infinity, and uniqueness of maximizers; those can be future work after the uniform calculation is fully certified.
concept.mathematical_framing: Borges' Library of Babel contains every possible 410-page book — approximately 25^{1312000} volumes. The library is finite but vast beyond comprehension. Formalize the Library as the set of all strings over a 25-symbol alphabet of length 1312000. Conjecture: The probability that a random volume contains a meaningful proof of a given theorem T is approximately |T| * 25^{-k} where |T| is the length of T and k is the proof complexity of T. Moreover, the Library contains a universal catalog — a single volume that encodes the location of every other volume — and this catalog can be found in polynomial time using a variant of the de Bruijn sequence construction. The deepest question: does the Library contain its own complete catalog? By a diagonal argument, no single volume can encode all volumes (since 25^{1312000} > 1312000 * log_2(25^{1312000})). But a DISTRIBUTED catalog spanning N volumes can encode the entire Library if N > 25^{1312000} / (1312000 * log_2(25)). Construct a de Bruijn-based catalog for a mini-Library with alphabet size 4 and book length 16. Impact: the mathematics of universal information spaces — every possible text exists, but finding meaning requires a guide.

import Mathlib
import Catalog.Algebra.LibraryOfBabel

/-!
# The Library of Babel as an ideal cryptographic entropy source

This file equips the Library of Babel (see `Catalog.Algebra.LibraryOfBabel`) with the
uniform probability distribution over its `b ^ L` volumes and studies its **Rényi
entropies** of arbitrary order `α`.

For a finite probability distribution `p : ι → ℝ` (with `∑ p i = 1`, `p i ≥ 0`) the Rényi
entropy of order `α` to base `b` is

* `H_α(p) = (1 - α)⁻¹ · log_b (∑ i, p i ^ α)` for `α ≠ 1`, and
* `H_1(p) = - ∑ i, p i · log_b (p i)` (the Shannon entropy) for `α = 1`,

where `x ^ α` denotes the real power `Real.rpow` and `log_b = Real.logb b`.

## Main results

* `renyiEntropy_uniform` : the uniform distribution on a nonempty finite type of
  cardinality `N` has Rényi entropy `log_b N` for **every** order `α` (this single
  computation simultaneously covers max-entropy `α = 0`, Shannon `α = 1`, collision
  `α = 2` and indeed all real orders).
* `renyiEntropy_uniform_library` : for an alphabet of size `b ≥ 2`, the uniform
  distribution on the `b ^ L` volumes has Rényi entropy exactly `L`, for every order
  `α`.  Thus all Rényi entropies coincide: the Library is a *perfect* (flat) entropy
  source.
* `minEntropy_uniform_library` : the min-entropy (`α = ∞`) likewise equals `L`.
* `renyiEntropy_zero_library` : the max-entropy (`α = 0`) equals `L` for **any**
  distribution supported on the volumes (it only sees the support size).
* `collisionEntropy_lt_of_ne_uniform` / `library_unique_maximal_entropy` : the uniform
  distribution is the **unique** maximiser of entropy on the support — any other
  distribution on the `b ^ L` volumes has strictly smaller collision entropy
  (`α = 2 > 0`), and hence is not maximal.
* concrete instantiations for the historical Borges parameters `b = 25`, `L = 1312000`.

The arguments are completely general in `b` and `L`; the value `L` is recovered from
`log_b (b ^ L)` precisely when `b ≥ 2` (for `b = 1` the library is a single volume and
the entropy is `0`).
-/

open Finset
open scoped Classical

namespace LibraryOfBabel

/-! ### Rényi entropy -/

/-- The Rényi entropy of order `α` (to base `b`) of a finite distribution `p`.
For `α = 1` this is the Shannon entropy `- ∑ p i · log_b (p i)`; otherwise it is
`(1 - α)⁻¹ · log_b (∑ p i ^ α)`, where the power is the real power `Real.rpow`. -/
noncomputable def renyiEntropy {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (b : ℝ) (p : ι → ℝ) (α : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  if α = 1 then - ∑ i, p i * Real.logb b (p i)
  else (1 - α)⁻¹ * Real.logb b (∑ i, (p i) ^ α)

/-- Collision entropy is the Rényi entropy of order `2`. -/
noncomputable def collisionEntropy {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (b : ℝ) (p : ι → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  renyiEntropy b p 2

/-- The min-entropy (`α = ∞`) of a finite distribution: `- log_b (max_i p i)`. -/
noncomputable def minEntropy {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (b : ℝ) (p : ι → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  - Real.logb b (⨆ i, p i)

/-! ### The Rényi entropy of the uniform distribution -/

/-- **Flatness of the uniform distribution.** For a nonempty finite type of cardinality
`N`, the uniform distribution `i ↦ N⁻¹` has Rényi entropy `log_b N` for *every* order
`α`.  In particular all Rényi entropies coincide. -/
theorem renyiEntropy_uniform {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι]
    (b : ℝ) (α : ℝ) :
    renyiEntropy b (fun _ : ι => (Fintype.card ι : ℝ)⁻¹) α
      = Real.logb b (Fintype.card ι) := by
  by_cases ha : α = 1 <;> simp_all +decide [renyiEntropy]
  rw [Real.inv_rpow (Nat.cast_nonneg _)]
  rw [← div_eq_inv_mul, Real.logb, Real.logb, Real.log_mul (by positivity) (by positivity),
    Real.log_inv, Real.log_rpow (by positivity), div_eq_iff]
  · ring
  · exact sub_ne_zero_of_ne (Ne.symm ha)

/-- The max-entropy (`α = 0`) of *any* distribution on a nonempty finite type is
`log_b N` (with the `rpow` convention `x ^ 0 = 1`, the order-`0` Rényi sum only sees the
support size). -/
theorem renyiEntropy_zero {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι]
    (b : ℝ) (p : ι → ℝ) :
    renyiEntropy b p 0 = Real.logb b (Fintype.card ι) := by
  unfold renyiEntropy; aesop

/-- The min-entropy of the uniform distribution equals `log_b N`. -/
theorem minEntropy_uniform {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] (b : ℝ) :
    minEntropy b (fun _ : ι => (Fintype.card ι : ℝ)⁻¹) = Real.logb b (Fintype.card ι) := by
  unfold minEntropy; aesop

/-! ### Specialisation to the Library of Babel -/

/-- The number of volumes equals `b ^ L`, as a statement about `Fintype.card`. -/
theorem card_volume (b L : ℕ) : Fintype.card (Volume b L) = b ^ L := by
  convert Fintype.card_fun; all_goals norm_num

/-- For an alphabet of size `b ≥ 2`, the uniform distribution on the `b ^ L` volumes
has Rényi entropy exactly `L`, for **every** order `α`.  All Rényi entropies coincide:
the Library of Babel is a perfect (flat) entropy source. -/
theorem renyiEntropy_uniform_library {b L : ℕ} (hb : 2 ≤ b) (α : ℝ) :
    renyiEntropy (b : ℝ) (fun _ : Volume b L => ((b ^ L : ℕ) : ℝ)⁻¹) α = L := by
  by_contra h_neq
  have h_uniform : renyiEntropy (b : ℝ) (fun _ : Volume b L => (Fintype.card (Volume b L) : ℝ)⁻¹) α
      = Real.logb (b : ℝ) (Fintype.card (Volume b L)) := by
    convert renyiEntropy_uniform b α using 1
    exact ⟨fun _ => ⟨0, by linarith⟩⟩
  simp_all +decide
  exact h_neq (by
    rw [Real.logb, Real.log_pow,
      mul_div_cancel_right₀ _ (ne_of_gt (Real.log_pos (by norm_cast)))])

/-- The min-entropy of the uniform library equals `L` (the `α = ∞` case). -/
theorem minEntropy_uniform_library {b L : ℕ} (hb : 2 ≤ b) :
    minEntropy (b : ℝ) (fun _ : Volume b L => ((b ^ L : ℕ) : ℝ)⁻¹) = L := by
  unfold minEntropy; norm_num
  rw [show (⨆ _ : Volume b L, (b ^ L : ℝ)⁻¹) = (b ^ L : ℝ)⁻¹ from ?_]
  · simp +decide [Real.logb, Real.log_pow]
    rw [neg_div, neg_neg, mul_div_cancel_right₀ _ (ne_of_gt (Real.log_pos (by norm_cast)))]
  · convert ciSup_const
    exact ⟨fun _ => ⟨0, by linarith⟩⟩

/-- The max-entropy (`α = 0`) of *any* distribution on the volumes equals `L`
(for `b ≥ 2`): all distributions on the support share the same order-`0` entropy. -/
theorem renyiEntropy_zero_library {b L : ℕ} (hb : 2 ≤ b) (p : Volume b L → ℝ) :
    renyiEntropy (b : ℝ) p 0 = L := by
  convert renyiEntropy_zero (b : ℝ) p using 1
  · rw [card_volume, Nat.cast_pow, Real.logb, Real.log_pow]
    rw [mul_div_cancel_right₀ _ (ne_of_gt (Real.log_pos (by norm_cast)))]
  · exact ⟨fun _ => ⟨0, by linarith⟩⟩

/-! ### Uniqueness of the uniform distribution as the maximiser of entropy -/

/-- **Key variance identity.** For any distribution `p` (with total mass `1`) on a
nonempty finite type of cardinality `N`, the collision sum `∑ p i ^ 2` exceeds its
minimal value `N⁻¹` exactly by the "variance" `∑ (p i - N⁻¹) ^ 2`. -/
theorem sum_sq_eq_uniform_add_variance {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι]
    (p : ι → ℝ) (hsum : ∑ i, p i = 1) :
    ∑ i, (p i) ^ 2
      = (Fintype.card ι : ℝ)⁻¹ + ∑ i, (p i - (Fintype.card ι : ℝ)⁻¹) ^ 2 := by
  simp +decide [sub_sq, Finset.sum_add_distrib]
  simp +decide [← Finset.mul_sum _ _ _, ← Finset.sum_mul, hsum, sq]
  ring

/-- **Strict sub-optimality of non-uniform distributions.** If `p` is a distribution
(`p i ≥ 0`, `∑ p i = 1`) on a nonempty finite type of cardinality `N`, with base
`b ≥ 2`, and `p` is *not* the uniform distribution, then its collision entropy is
strictly below the flat value `log_b N`.

The nonnegativity hypothesis `_hnonneg` is kept to reflect that `p` is a genuine
probability distribution as in the statement of the problem, but it is not actually
needed by the proof: the strict bound holds for any real weights summing to `1`. -/
theorem collisionEntropy_lt_of_ne_uniform {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι]
    {b : ℝ} (hb : 2 ≤ b) (p : ι → ℝ) (_hnonneg : ∀ i, 0 ≤ p i)
    (hsum : ∑ i, p i = 1) (hne : p ≠ fun _ => (Fintype.card ι : ℝ)⁻¹) :
    collisionEntropy b p < Real.logb b (Fintype.card ι) := by
  unfold collisionEntropy
  norm_num [renyiEntropy]
  rw [← Real.logb_inv, Real.logb_lt_logb_iff]
  · have h_var : ∑ i, (p i - (Fintype.card ι : ℝ)⁻¹) ^ 2 > 0 :=
      lt_of_le_of_ne (Finset.sum_nonneg fun _ _ => sq_nonneg _)
        (Ne.symm <| by
          contrapose! hne; ext i
          simp_all +decide [sub_eq_iff_eq_add, Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg, sq_nonneg])
    convert inv_strictAnti₀ _ (show ∑ i, p i ^ 2 > (Fintype.card ι : ℝ)⁻¹ from _) using 1
    · norm_num
    · exact inv_pos.mpr (Nat.cast_pos.mpr Fintype.card_pos)
    · convert sum_sq_eq_uniform_add_variance p hsum |> fun h => h.symm ▸ lt_add_of_pos_right _ h_var
        using 1
  · linarith
  · exact inv_pos.mpr (lt_of_le_of_ne (Finset.sum_nonneg fun _ _ => sq_nonneg _)
      (Ne.symm <| by
        intro h
        exact hne <| funext fun i => by
          rw [Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg fun _ _ => sq_nonneg _] at h; aesop))
  · exact Nat.cast_pos.mpr Fintype.card_pos

/-- **Uniqueness of the maximal-entropy distribution on the Library.** The uniform
distribution attains collision entropy `L`, and every *other* distribution on the
`b ^ L` volumes has strictly smaller collision entropy. Hence the uniform distribution
is the unique maximiser of (Rényi) entropy on the support. -/
theorem library_unique_maximal_entropy {b L : ℕ} (hb : 2 ≤ b)
    (p : Volume b L → ℝ) (hnonneg : ∀ v, 0 ≤ p v) (hsum : ∑ v, p v = 1)
    (hne : p ≠ fun _ => ((b ^ L : ℕ) : ℝ)⁻¹) :
    collisionEntropy (b : ℝ) p < L := by
  have := @collisionEntropy_lt_of_ne_uniform (Volume b L)
  convert this (show 2 ≤ (b : ℝ) by norm_cast) p hnonneg hsum _ using 1
  · rw [show Fintype.card (Volume b L) = b ^ L from card_volume b L]
    norm_num [Real.logb, hb]
    rw [mul_div_cancel_right₀ _ (ne_of_gt (Real.log_pos (by norm_cast)))]
  · exact ⟨fun _ => ⟨0, by linarith⟩⟩
  · convert hne using 3; norm_num [card_volume]

/-! ### Concrete Borges parameters `b = 25`, `L = 1312000` -/

/-- The Borges library (`b = 25`, `L = 1312000`) has the same Rényi entropy `1312000`
for every order `α`. -/
theorem renyiEntropy_borges (α : ℝ) :
    renyiEntropy (25 : ℝ)
      (fun _ : Volume 25 1312000 => ((25 ^ 1312000 : ℕ) : ℝ)⁻¹) α = 1312000 := by
  convert renyiEntropy_uniform_library (by norm_num : 2 ≤ 25) α using 1

/-- The Borges library has min-entropy `1312000`. -/
theorem minEntropy_borges :
    minEntropy (25 : ℝ)
      (fun _ : Volume 25 1312000 => ((25 ^ 1312000 : ℕ) : ℝ)⁻¹) = 1312000 := by
  convert minEntropy_uniform_library (by norm_num : 2 ≤ 25)

/-- Any non-uniform distribution on the Borges volumes has strictly smaller collision
entropy than the uniform value `1312000`. -/
theorem borges_unique_maximal_entropy
    (p : Volume 25 1312000 → ℝ) (hnonneg : ∀ v, 0 ≤ p v) (hsum : ∑ v, p v = 1)
    (hne : p ≠ fun _ => ((25 ^ 1312000 : ℕ) : ℝ)⁻¹) :
    collisionEntropy (25 : ℝ) p < 1312000 :=
  library_unique_maximal_entropy (by norm_num) p hnonneg hsum hne

end LibraryOfBabel

import Mathlib
import MachineLearning.CechComplex

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory

namespace SheafDatabaseProbability

/-! ## §1. The product law: probability that all overlap constraints hold -/

variable {Ω ι : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : Measure Ω}

/-- **Sheaf-condition product law.**  Model each overlapping consistency
constraint as an event `f i`.  If the constraints are independent and each holds
with the same probability `q`, then the probability that *all* of them hold (the
database glues to a global section) is `q ^ |s|`. -/
theorem sheaf_consistency_prob_eq_pow
    {f : ι → Set Ω} (hindep : iIndepSet f μ) (s : Finset ι)
    (q : ENNReal) (hq : ∀ i ∈ s, μ (f i) = q) :
    μ (⋂ i ∈ s, f i) = q ^ s.card := by
  rw [hindep.meas_biInter s, Finset.prod_congr rfl hq, Finset.prod_const]

/-- **Missing-rate form.**  Writing the per-constraint success probability as
`q = 1 - r` for a missing/inconsistency rate `r ∈ [0,1]`, the probability of
consistent imputation is `(1 - r) ^ |s|`. -/
theorem sheaf_consistency_prob_missing_rate
    {f : ι → Set Ω} (hindep : iIndepSet f μ) (s : Finset ι)
    (r : ℝ) (hr1 : r ≤ 1)
    (hmiss : ∀ i ∈ s, μ (f i) = ENNReal.ofReal (1 - r)) :
    μ (⋂ i ∈ s, f i) = ENNReal.ofReal ((1 - r) ^ s.card) := by
  rw [sheaf_consistency_prob_eq_pow hindep s _ hmiss,
    ENNReal.ofReal_pow (by linarith)]

/-- **Headline conjecture `P(sheaf) = (1 - r)^{C(n,k)}`.**  When the number of
overlapping constraints equals the binomial count `C(n,k) = n.choose k`, the
probability of consistent imputation is `(1 - r) ^ C(n,k)`. -/
theorem sheaf_consistency_prob_choose
    {f : ι → Set Ω} (hindep : iIndepSet f μ) (s : Finset ι)
    (n k : ℕ) (hcard : s.card = n.choose k)
    (r : ℝ) (hr1 : r ≤ 1)
    (hmiss : ∀ i ∈ s, μ (f i) = ENNReal.ofReal (1 - r)) :
    μ (⋂ i ∈ s, f i) = ENNReal.ofReal ((1 - r) ^ (n.choose k)) := by
  rw [sheaf_consistency_prob_missing_rate hindep s r hr1 hmiss, hcard]

/-! ## §2. Exponential decay of consistency with the number of constraints -/

/-- **Exponential decay (monotonicity).**  Adding overlapping constraints can
only *lower* the probability of global consistency: `(1-r)^n ≤ (1-r)^m` for
`m ≤ n`.  This is the precise sense in which "consistent imputation drops
exponentially with the number of overlapping constraints". -/
theorem sheaf_prob_antitone (r : ℝ) (hr0 : 0 ≤ r) (hr1 : r ≤ 1)
    {m n : ℕ} (hmn : m ≤ n) :
    (1 - r) ^ n ≤ (1 - r) ^ m :=
  pow_le_pow_of_le_one (by linarith) (by linarith) hmn

/-- **Any positive missing rate makes consistency uncertain.**  With `r > 0` and
at least one constraint, the probability of consistent imputation is strictly
below `1`: a global section is never guaranteed. -/
theorem sheaf_prob_lt_one (r : ℝ) (hr0 : 0 < r) (hr1 : r ≤ 1) {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) :
    (1 - r) ^ n < 1 :=
  pow_lt_one₀ (by linarith) (by linarith) (by omega)

/-- **Collapse to zero.**  As the number of overlapping constraints grows, the
probability of consistent imputation tends to `0` (for any positive missing
rate).  Exponentially many consistency constraints make global gluing
asymptotically impossible by chance. -/
theorem sheaf_prob_tendsto_zero (r : ℝ) (hr0 : 0 < r) (hr1 : r ≤ 1) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n => (1 - r) ^ n) Filter.atTop (nhds 0) :=
  tendsto_pow_atTop_nhds_zero_of_lt_one (by linarith) (by linarith)

/-! ## §3. Bridge to Čech cohomology: sheaf imputation is path independent -/

/-- **Sheaf imputation is path independent.**  Model imputed column values as a
Čech `0`-cochain `f`; the imputed pairwise overlap discrepancies are the
coboundary `δ⁰ f`.  Being a coboundary, they form a cocycle and therefore obey
the Čech triangle identity

  `(δ⁰f)(i,j) + (δ⁰f)(j,l) + (δ⁰f)(l,i) = 0`,

i.e. the imputed difference between any two columns is independent of the path
taken through intermediate columns.  This is the deterministic gluing law
underlying the probabilistic sheaf condition above, and it is proved by
combining `coboundary_is_cocycle` with `cocycle_triangle_sum_zero` from
`MachineLearning.CechComplex`. -/
theorem imputation_path_independent (m : ℕ) (f : CechCausalComplex.CechZeroCochain m)
    (i j l : Fin m) :
    CechCausalComplex.coboundaryZero m f i j
      + CechCausalComplex.coboundaryZero m f j l
      + CechCausalComplex.coboundaryZero m f l i = 0 := by
  have hcocycle : CechCausalComplex.IsOneCocycle m (CechCausalComplex.coboundaryZero m f) :=
    CechCausalComplex.coboundary_is_cocycle m _ ⟨f, rfl⟩
  exact CechCausalComplex.cocycle_triangle_sum_zero m _ hcocycle i j l

end SheafDatabaseProbability

Companion to `MachineLearning.SheafDatabaseProbability`.  Where that file computes
the probability `P(sheaf) = (1-r)^{N}` that **all** overlap constraints hold, this
file quantifies the *failure* event (the sheaf condition is violated, so the
database cannot be consistently glued) and gives sharp two-sided linear bounds.

## Main results

* `sheaf_failure_prob_eq` — exact failure probability:
  `μ ((⋂ i∈s, f i)ᶜ) = 1 - q ^ |s|` for independent constraint events of
  common probability `q`.
* `sheaf_consistency_ge_linear` — Bernoulli lower bound:
  `1 - n·r ≤ (1 - r)^n`; for a small constraint budget `n·r`, consistency is
  likely (a quantitative "easy regime").
* `sheaf_failure_le_linear` — union bound:
  `1 - (1 - r)^n ≤ n·r`; the failure probability never exceeds the naive sum of
  per-constraint failure rates.
* `sheaf_failure_pos` — with `r > 0` and `n ≥ 1`, failure has positive
  probability: imputation is genuinely uncertain.

## Cross-domain note
The exact `sheaf_failure_prob_eq` is the measure-theoretic complement of the
product law (`prob_compl_eq_one_sub`), while the linear bounds are the analytic
Bernoulli/union inequalities that govern the small-`r` regime where sheaf
imputation is expected to dominate naive methods.

import Mathlib

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory

namespace SheafImputationBounds

/-! ## §1. Exact failure probability (measure-theoretic complement) -/

variable {Ω ι : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]

/-- **Exact failure probability.**  For independent, measurable constraint events
`f i` of common probability `q`, the probability that the sheaf condition *fails*
(at least one overlap constraint is violated, so no global section exists) is
`1 - q ^ |s|`. -/
theorem sheaf_failure_prob_eq
    {f : ι → Set Ω} (hindep : iIndepSet f μ) (hmeas : ∀ i, MeasurableSet (f i))
    (s : Finset ι) (q : ENNReal) (hq : ∀ i ∈ s, μ (f i) = q) :
    μ (⋂ i ∈ s, f i)ᶜ = 1 - q ^ s.card := by
  have hms : MeasurableSet (⋂ i ∈ s, f i) :=
    MeasurableSet.biInter s.countable_toSet (fun i _ => hmeas i)
  rw [prob_compl_eq_one_sub hms, hindep.meas_biInter s, Finset.prod_congr rfl hq,
    Finset.prod_const]

/-! ## §2. Two-sided linear bounds (Bernoulli / union) -/

/-- **Bernoulli lower bound (easy regime).**  The probability of consistent
imputation is at least `1 - n·r`.  Hence when the *constraint budget* `n·r` is
small, a global section almost surely exists. -/
theorem sheaf_consistency_ge_linear (r : ℝ) (hr1 : r ≤ 1) (n : ℕ) :
    1 - n * r ≤ (1 - r) ^ n := by
  have h := one_add_mul_le_pow (a := -r) (by linarith) n
  simpa [sub_eq_add_neg, mul_comm, mul_neg] using h

/-- **Union bound on failure.**  The probability that the sheaf condition fails is
at most `n·r`, the naive sum of the per-constraint missing rates.  This is the
real-analytic shadow of the measure-theoretic union bound. -/
theorem sheaf_failure_le_linear (r : ℝ) (hr1 : r ≤ 1) (n : ℕ) :
    1 - (1 - r) ^ n ≤ n * r := by
  have h := sheaf_consistency_ge_linear r hr1 n
  linarith

/-- **Failure is genuinely possible.**  With a positive missing rate `r > 0` and
at least one constraint, the failure probability `1 - (1 - r)^n` is strictly
positive: consistent imputation can never be guaranteed by chance. -/
theorem sheaf_failure_pos (r : ℝ) (hr0 : 0 < r) (hr1 : r ≤ 1) {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) :
    0 < 1 - (1 - r) ^ n := by
  have h : (1 - r) ^ n < 1 := pow_lt_one₀ (by linarith) (by linarith) (by omega)
  linarith

end SheafImputationBounds

import Mathlib

/-!
# An Anti-Gravity (divisor-dependency) model

This file formalises a small "divisor-dependency" model.  We imagine a library of
`N` theorems indexed `1, 2, …, N`.  A theorem `d` *supports* every multiple of `d`
in the library, so its **support weight** is the number of multiples of `d` in the
range `[1, N]`, namely the floor division `N / d`.

The **proof cost** of `d` is the number of prime factors of `d` counted with
multiplicity, i.e. the length of its prime-factorisation list.  Short proofs
correspond to numbers with few prime factors (in the extreme, primes, which have
cost `1`).

The central observation ("anti-gravity tension") is that support weight decays at
least exponentially in proof cost:

  `support N d ≤ N / 2 ^ proofCost d`,

because `2 ^ proofCost d ≤ d`.  Primes are the extremal "anti-gravity theorems":
they have the smallest possible positive proof cost (`1`) and the largest possible
support `N / p` for that cost.

## Main results

* `support_eq_div`            : the support weight equals `N / d`.
* `two_pow_proofCost_le`      : `2 ^ proofCost d ≤ d`.
* `support_le_div_two_pow`    : `support N d ≤ N / 2 ^ proofCost d`.
* `prime_isAntiGravity`       : every prime `p ≤ N` has `proofCost p = 1` and
                                support `N / p`.
* `tightness_of_bound`        : the exponential bound is attained (witness `d = 2`).
* `antiGravity_weight_unbounded` : short-proof theorems achieve arbitrarily large
                                support.
* `antiGravity_main`          : a bundle of all of the above.
-/

namespace AntiGravity

/-- The **support weight** of theorem `d` in a library of size `N`: the number of
multiples of `d` in `[1, N]`, given by floor division `N / d`. -/
def support (N d : ℕ) : ℕ := N / d

/-- The **proof cost** of `d`: the number of prime factors of `d` counted with
multiplicity (the length of its prime-factorisation list).  In particular primes
have cost `1` and `1` has cost `0`. -/
def proofCost (d : ℕ) : ℕ := (Nat.primeFactorsList d).length

/-- Auxiliary inequality: if every entry of a list of naturals is at least `2`, then
`2` raised to the length of the list is at most the product of the list. -/
lemma two_pow_length_le_prod (L : List ℕ) (h : ∀ x ∈ L, 2 ≤ x) :
    2 ^ L.length ≤ L.prod := by
  simpa using List.prod_le_prod' h

/-- **Exact weight formula.** The support weight is exactly `N / d` (floor
division).  The hypothesis `1 ≤ d` is part of the requested interface; the equality
holds definitionally and does not in fact require it. -/
theorem support_eq_div (N d : ℕ) (h : 1 ≤ d) : support N d = N / d := by
  rfl

/-- **The exponential of the proof cost never exceeds the number itself.**
Since `d` is the product of its (≥ 2) prime factors and `proofCost d` counts them,
`2 ^ proofCost d ≤ d`. -/
theorem two_pow_proofCost_le (d : ℕ) (h : d ≠ 0) : 2 ^ proofCost d ≤ d := by
  refine le_trans (two_pow_length_le_prod _ fun x hx =>
    (Nat.prime_of_mem_primeFactorsList hx).two_le) ?_
  simp [Nat.prod_primeFactorsList h]

/-- **Anti-gravity tension theorem.** Support weight decays at least exponentially
in proof length: `support N d ≤ N / 2 ^ proofCost d`. -/
theorem support_le_div_two_pow (N d : ℕ) (h : 1 ≤ d) :
    support N d ≤ N / 2 ^ proofCost d := by
  exact Nat.div_le_div_left (two_pow_proofCost_le d (by positivity)) (by positivity)

/-- **Every prime `p ≤ N` is an anti-gravity theorem.** Its proof cost is `1` and
its support is `N / p`.  (The hypothesis `p ≤ N`, requested in the interface, is the
"in the library" condition; the conclusions hold for any prime `p`.) -/
theorem prime_isAntiGravity (p N : ℕ) (hp : Nat.Prime p) (hpN : p ≤ N) :
    proofCost p = 1 ∧ support N p = N / p := by
  refine ⟨?_, rfl⟩
  simp [proofCost, Nat.primeFactorsList_prime hp]

/-- **Tightness of the bound.** The exponential bound `support N d ≤ N / 2 ^ proofCost d`
is attained: with the witness `d = 2` (a prime, so proof cost `1`) the support equals
`N / 2 = N / 2 ^ proofCost 2`.

Note: the original informal statement omitted a hypothesis on `N`.  As stated it is
*false* for `N ≤ 1`, since then there is no `d ≤ N` with `proofCost d = 1`
(equivalently, no prime `≤ N`).  We therefore add the necessary hypothesis
`2 ≤ N`. -/
theorem tightness_of_bound (N : ℕ) (hN : 2 ≤ N) :
    ∃ d ≤ N, proofCost d = 1 ∧ support N d = N / 2 := by
  exact ⟨2, hN, by simp [proofCost, Nat.primeFactorsList_prime Nat.prime_two], rfl⟩

/-- **Density-type analogue / unboundedness of weight.** For any target weight `w`
there is a library size `N` and a short-proof theorem `d` (proof cost `1`) whose
support is at least `w`. -/
theorem antiGravity_weight_unbounded :
    ∀ w : ℕ, ∃ N d, 1 ≤ d ∧ proofCost d = 1 ∧ support N d ≥ w := by
  intro w
  exact ⟨2 * w, 2, by norm_num,
    by simp [proofCost, Nat.primeFactorsList_prime Nat.prime_two],
    by simp [support]⟩

/-- **Bundle.** All of the main anti-gravity results collected into a single
statement. -/
theorem antiGravity_main :
    (∀ N d, 1 ≤ d → support N d = N / d) ∧
    (∀ d, d ≠ 0 → 2 ^ proofCost d ≤ d) ∧
    (∀ N d, 1 ≤ d → support N d ≤ N / 2 ^ proofCost d) ∧
    (∀ p N, Nat.Prime p → p ≤ N → proofCost p = 1 ∧ support N p = N / p) ∧
    (∀ N, 2 ≤ N → ∃ d ≤ N, proofCost d = 1 ∧ support N d = N / 2) ∧
    (∀ w : ℕ, ∃ N d, 1 ≤ d ∧ proofCost d = 1 ∧ support N d ≥ w) :=
  ⟨support_eq_div, two_pow_proofCost_le, support_le_div_two_pow, prime_isAntiGravity,
    tightness_of_bound, antiGravity_weight_unbounded⟩

end AntiGravity

* `pow_rowStochastic`: Powers of row-stochastic matrices are row-stochastic.
* `positive_triangleCyc_of_mixing_bound`: Existence of a mixing bound

arbitrary positive row-stochastic matrices with uniform mixing convergence.

`triangleCyc ≈ -log(0.99) ≈ 0.01 < log(2) ≈ 0.69`.

Row-stochastic matrices have power entries bounded above by 1.

    intro m i; induction' m with m ih generalizing i <;> simp_all +decide [ pow_succ', Matrix.mul_apply, Finset.mul_sum _ _ _ ] ;

    · rw [ Finset.sum_comm ];

  exact h_row_sum m i ▸ Finset.single_le_sum ( fun a _ => show 0 ≤ ( P ^ m ) i a from by

Row sums are preserved under matrix powers.
-/

    (P : Matrix (Fin (n+1)) (Fin (n+1)) ℝ)
    (hrow : RowStochastic P) (m : ℕ) (i : Fin (n+1)) :
    ∑ j, (P ^ m) i j = 1 := by
  have h_sum_transpose : ∀ m : ℕ, ∀ i : Fin (n + 1), ∑ j, (P ^ m) i j = 1 := by
    intro m i; induction' m with m ih generalizing i <;> simp_all +decide [ pow_succ', Matrix.mul_apply, Finset.mul_sum _ _ _, Finset.sum_mul ] ;
    · simp +decide [ Matrix.one_apply ];
    · rw [ Finset.sum_comm ];

  convert h_sum_transpose m i using 1

    (hrow : RowStochastic P) (m : ℕ) :

**Positivity from mixing.**

probabilities are at most `α`, then the tropical cycle mean is
strictly positive.

probabilities can decay. For any `m ≥ 1`, the best achievable uniform

-/

    (α : ℝ) (hα : 0 < α) (hα1 : α < 1)

This module formalizes the **compositional certified robustness principle**:

difference `f_y - f_j` is affine. The **local radius** is the largest ball around `x₀`

/-- The global certified radius: every point within distance `r` of `x₀` preserves

def GlobalCertified {n k : ℕ} (f : (Fin n → ℝ) → (Fin k → ℝ))
    (x₀ : Fin n → ℝ) (y : Fin k) (r : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Fin n → ℝ, ‖x - x₀‖ < r → ∀ j : Fin k, f x y ≥ f x j

    all points in `R` within distance `r` of `x₀`. -/

    (x₀ : Fin n → ℝ) (y : Fin k) (R : Set (Fin n → ℝ)) (r : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Fin n → ℝ, x ∈ R → ‖x - x₀‖ < r → ∀ j : Fin k, f x y ≥ f x j

/-- The region radius: the open ball of radius `r` around `x₀` is contained in `R`. -/

  ∃ j : Fin k, j ≠ y ∧ ∃ x : Fin n → ℝ, ‖x - x₀‖ = r ∧ f x y = f x j

    (x₀ : Fin n → ℝ) (y : Fin k) (R : Set (Fin n → ℝ)) (r : ℝ) : Prop :=

  apply le_tropFactorRank

/-- **Tropical Factor Rank Encoding Theorem.**
    For every natural number `s`, the `s × s` tropical identity-like matrix

theorem tropFactorRank_encodeDiag (s : ℕ) :
    tropFactorRank (encodeDiag s) = s :=
  le_antisymm (tropFactorRank_encodeDiag_le s) (tropFactorRank_encodeDiag_ge s)

theorem tropFactorRank_surjective :
    Function.Surjective (fun s => @tropFactorRank s (encodeDiag s)) :=
  fun s => ⟨s, tropFactorRank_encodeDiag s⟩

/-! ## Section 1: Core Definitions -/

/-- The global certified radius: every point within distance `r` of `x₀` preserves
    class `y` as the argmax of `f`. -/
def GlobalCertified {n k : ℕ} (f : (Fin n → ℝ) → (Fin k → ℝ))
    (x₀ : Fin n → ℝ) (y : Fin k) (r : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Fin n → ℝ, ‖x - x₀‖ < r → ∀ j : Fin k, f x y ≥ f x j

/-- The local certified radius on a region `R`: classification is preserved for
    all points in `R` within distance `r` of `x₀`. -/
def LocalCertified {n k : ℕ} (f : (Fin n → ℝ) → (Fin k → ℝ))
    (x₀ : Fin n → ℝ) (y : Fin k) (R : Set (Fin n → ℝ)) (r : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Fin n → ℝ, x ∈ R → ‖x - x₀‖ < r → ∀ j : Fin k, f x y ≥ f x j

/-- The region radius: the open ball of radius `r` around `x₀` is contained in `R`. -/
def RegionContains {n : ℕ} (x₀ : Fin n → ℝ) (R : Set (Fin n → ℝ)) (r : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Fin n → ℝ, ‖x - x₀‖ < r → x ∈ R

/-- A witness for tightness of the local radius: there exists a point on
    the margin boundary at exactly distance `r_local`. -/
def MarginTight {n k : ℕ} (f : (Fin n → ℝ) → (Fin k → ℝ))
    (x₀ : Fin n → ℝ) (y : Fin k) (r : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ j : Fin k, j ≠ y ∧ ∃ x : Fin n → ℝ, ‖x - x₀‖ = r ∧ f x y = f x j

/-- A witness for tightness of the region radius: there exists a boundary
    point at exactly distance `r_region` where crossing leads to class change. -/
def RegionTight {n k : ℕ} (f : (Fin n → ℝ) → (Fin k → ℝ))
    (x₀ : Fin n → ℝ) (y : Fin k) (R : Set (Fin n → ℝ)) (r : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ x : Fin n → ℝ, ‖x - x₀‖ = r ∧ x ∉ R ∧
    ∃ j : Fin k, j ≠ y ∧ f x j > f x y

/-! ## Section 2: Core Compositional Bound -/

/-
**Main theorem: Compositional certified radius lower bound.**

If `r_local` is a local certified radius within region `R`, and `r_region` ensures
the ball stays inside `R`, then classification is preserved within `min(r_local, r_region)`.

This is the key decomposition: robustness = min(margin safety, region stability).
-/
theorem global_radius_ge_min_local_region
    {n k : ℕ}
    (f : (Fin n → ℝ) → (Fin k → ℝ))
    (x₀ : Fin n → ℝ)
    (y : Fin k)
    (R : Set (Fin n → ℝ))
    (r_local r_region : ℝ)
    (hlocal : LocalCertified f x₀ y R r_local)
    (hregion : RegionContains x₀ R r_region) :
    GlobalCertified f x₀ y (min r_local r_region) := by
  grind +locals

/-
Monotonicity: if `GlobalCertified` holds at radius `r`, it holds for any smaller radius.
-/
theorem GlobalCertified.mono {n k : ℕ} {f : (Fin n → ℝ) → (Fin k → ℝ)}
    {x₀ : Fin n → ℝ} {y : Fin k} {r s : ℝ} (h : GlobalCertified f x₀ y r) (hrs : s ≤ r) :
    GlobalCertified f x₀ y s := by
  -- By definition of GlobalCertified, if ‖x - x₀‖ < s ≤ r, then ‖x - x₀‖ < r, so we can apply h.
  intros x hx j; exact h x (by linarith [hx]) j

/-
Monotonicity for local certificates.
-/
theorem LocalCertified.mono {n k : ℕ} {f : (Fin n → ℝ) → (Fin k → ℝ)}
    {x₀ : Fin n → ℝ} {y : Fin k} {R : Set (Fin n → ℝ)} {r s : ℝ}
    (h : LocalCertified f x₀ y R r) (hrs : s ≤ r) :
    LocalCertified f x₀ y R s := by
  exact fun x hx hx' j => h x hx ( lt_of_lt_of_le hx' hrs ) j

/-
A local certificate on the whole space is a global certificate.
-/
theorem LocalCertified.to_global {n k : ℕ} {f : (Fin n → ℝ) → (Fin k → ℝ)}
    {x₀ : Fin n → ℝ} {y : Fin k} {r : ℝ}
    (h : LocalCertified f x₀ y Set.univ r) :
    GlobalCertified f x₀ y r := by
  exact fun x hx j => h x trivial hx j

/-! ## Section 3: Exact Radius Characterization -/

/-
**Equality characterization**: the global certified radius equals
    `min(r_local, r_region)` when the appropriate tightness condition holds.

    The `hglobal_def` hypothesis asserts that no larger radius works as a global
    certificate, making the bound tight. The tightness conditions explain *why*
    the bound is tight: either a margin tie (inside the region) or a region escape
    (at the boundary) is the first obstruction.
-/
theorem exact_global_radius_eq_min
    {n k : ℕ}
    (f : (Fin n → ℝ) → (Fin k → ℝ))
    (x₀ : Fin n → ℝ)
    (y : Fin k)
    (R : Set (Fin n → ℝ))
    (r_local r_region : ℝ)
    (hr_local_pos : r_local > 0)
    (hr_region_pos : r_region > 0)
    (hlocal : LocalCertified f x₀ y R r_local)
    (hregion : RegionContains x₀ R r_region)
    (htight_local : r_local ≤ r_region → MarginTight f x₀ y r_local)
    (htight_region : r_region ≤ r_local → RegionTight f x₀ y R r_region)
    (hglobal_def : ∀ r, GlobalCertified f x₀ y r → r ≤ min r_local r_region) :
    ∀ r, GlobalCertified f x₀ y r ↔ r ≤ min r_local r_region := by
  refine' fun r => ⟨ hglobal_def r, fun hr => _ ⟩;
  exact GlobalCertified.mono ( global_radius_ge_min_local_region f x₀ y R r_local r_region hlocal hregion ) hr

/-! ## Section 4: Tropical Lipschitz Local Certificate -/

/-
**Bridge to tropical spectral bounds**: If the network has Lipschitz constant
    `K` and tropical degree `d`, then the pairwise tropical certificate radius
    provides a local certificate on any region.
-/
theorem tropical_local_certificate
    {n k : ℕ}
    (f : (Fin n → ℝ) → (Fin k → ℝ))
    (x₀ : Fin n → ℝ) (y : Fin k)
    (R : Set (Fin n → ℝ))
    (K : ℝ≥0) (hK : 0 < K)
    (hlip : ∀ j, LipschitzWith K (fun x => f x j))
    (d : ℕ) (hd : 1 ≤ d)
    (hcorrect : ∀ j, j ≠ y → f x₀ y > f x₀ j)
    (hx₀ : x₀ ∈ R)
    (r : ℝ) (hr : r > 0)
    (hr_bound : ∀ j, j ≠ y → r ≤ (f x₀ y - f x₀ j) / (2 * K * d)) :
    LocalCertified f x₀ y R r := by
  intro x hx hx' j; by_cases hj : j = y <;> simp_all +decide [ div_le_iff₀ ] ;
  -- Apply the Lipschitz property to get the bounds on the differences.
  have h_lip : ‖f x y - f x₀ y‖ ≤ K * ‖x - x₀‖ ∧ ‖f x j - f x₀ j‖ ≤ K * ‖x - x₀‖ := by
    exact ⟨ by simpa using hlip y |>.dist_le_mul x x₀, by simpa using hlip j |>.dist_le_mul x x₀ ⟩;
  have := hr_bound j hj;
  rw [ le_div_iff₀ ] at this <;> norm_num at *;
  · nlinarith [ abs_le.mp h_lip.1, abs_le.mp h_lip.2, show ( d : ℝ ) ≥ 1 by norm_cast, show ( K : ℝ ) > 0 by positivity, mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left ( show ( d : ℝ ) ≥ 1 by norm_cast ) ( show ( K : ℝ ) ≥ 0 by positivity ) ];
  · positivity

/-
**Full compositional theorem with tropical certificates.**

Combines `tropical_local_certificate` with the region containment
to get a global certified radius from tropical spectral data.
-/
theorem tropical_compositional_certified_radius
    {n k : ℕ}
    (f : (Fin n → ℝ) → (Fin k → ℝ))
    (x₀ : Fin n → ℝ) (y : Fin k)
    (R : Set (Fin n → ℝ))
    (K : ℝ≥0) (hK : 0 < K)
    (hlip : ∀ j, LipschitzWith K (fun x => f x j))
    (d : ℕ) (hd : 1 ≤ d)
    (hcorrect : ∀ j, j ≠ y → f x₀ y > f x₀ j)
    (hx₀ : x₀ ∈ R)
    (r_local : ℝ) (hr_local : r_local > 0)
    (hr_local_bound : ∀ j, j ≠ y → r_local ≤ (f x₀ y - f x₀ j) / (2 * K * d))
    (r_region : ℝ)
    (hregion : RegionContains x₀ R r_region) :
    GlobalCertified f x₀ y (min r_local r_region) := by
  apply global_radius_ge_min_local_region f x₀ y R r_local r_region (by
  convert tropical_local_certificate f x₀ y R K hK hlip d hd hcorrect hx₀ r_local hr_local hr_local_bound) hregion

/-! ## Section 5: Lipschitz Global Certificate -/

/-
The Lipschitz certificate: within radius `gap / (2K)` for each competing class,
    the classification is preserved.
-/
theorem lipschitz_cert_is_global {n k : ℕ}
    (f : (Fin n → ℝ) → (Fin k → ℝ))
    (x₀ : Fin n → ℝ) (y : Fin k) (K : ℝ≥0) (hK : K > 0)
    (hlip : ∀ j, LipschitzWith K (fun x => f x j))
    (hcorrect : ∀ j, j ≠ y → f x₀ y > f x₀ j)
    (r : ℝ) (hr : r > 0)
    (hr_bound : ∀ j, j ≠ y → r ≤ (f x₀ y - f x₀ j) / (2 * K)) :
    GlobalCertified f x₀ y r := by
  -- For any $x$ with $\|x - x₀\| < r$, we have $|f x y - f x₀ y| \leq K \|x - x₀\|$ and $|f x j - f x₀ j| \leq K \|x - x₀\|$ for all $j$.
  have h_lip : ∀ x, ‖x - x₀‖ < r → ∀ j, |f x j - f x₀ j| ≤ K * ‖x - x₀‖ := by
    exact fun x hx j => by simpa using hlip j |>.dist_le_mul x x₀;
  -- Therefore, $2K \|x - x₀\| < f x₀ y - f x₀ j$, which implies $f x y - f x j > 0$.
  intros x hx
  by_cases hxy : x = x₀;
  · grind +splitImp;
  · intro j; specialize hr_bound j; by_cases hj : j = y <;> simp_all +decide [ le_div_iff₀, mul_assoc ] ;
    nlinarith [ abs_le.mp ( h_lip x hx j ), abs_le.mp ( h_lip x hx y ), hcorrect j hj, show ( K : ℝ ) > 0 by positivity ]

end

# Computational Evidence — Erdős–Rényi G(n,p)

This note records the small-case sanity checks that guided the formalization in
`Model.lean`, `SecondMoment.lean`, and `SubgraphCounting.lean`.

## 1. The weights are a probability distribution

For edge type `E` with `|E| = m`, the configuration space `E → Bool` has `2^m`
elements and `∑_ω weight(ω) = ∏_e (p + (1-p)) = 1` for every `p`.

| m | #configs | ∑ weight (any p) |
|---|----------|------------------|
| 1 | 2        | p + (1-p) = 1    |
| 2 | 4        | (p+(1-p))² = 1   |
| 3 | 8        | 1                |

This is the content of `sum_weight` (a polynomial identity, hence proved with no
constraint on `p`).

## 2. Expected edge count `𝔼[#edges] = C(n,2)·p`

`K_n` has `C(n,2)` potential edges, each present with probability `p`, so by
linearity the expected number of edges is `C(n,2)·p`.

| n | C(n,2) | 𝔼[#edges] |
|---|--------|-----------|
| 2 | 1      | p         |
| 3 | 3      | 3p        |
| 4 | 6      | 6p        |
| 5 | 10     | 10p       |

Formalized as `expect_edgeCount`.

## 3. Expected triangle count `𝔼[#triangles] = C(n,3)·p³`

Each of the `C(n,3)` vertex triples forms a triangle iff its three edges are all
present, an event of probability `p³` (edge independence).

| n | C(n,3) | 𝔼[#triangles] |
|---|--------|----------------|
| 3 | 1      | p³             |
| 4 | 4      | 4p³            |
| 5 | 10     | 10p³           |
| 6 | 20     | 20p³           |

Formalized as `expect_triangleCount`.

## 4. The first-moment threshold for triangles

Set `p = c/n`. Then `𝔼[#triangles] = C(n,3)·p³ ≈ (n³/6)(c³/n³) = c³/6`, a
constant. For `c³/6 < 1` (i.e. `c < 6^{1/3} ≈ 1.817`) the expected count is `< 1`,
so by Markov a positive fraction of graphs are triangle-free.  This pins the
threshold for triangle appearance at `p ≍ n^{-1}`.

Sample (the exact finite criterion `C(n,3)·p³ < 1` used by `triangle_threshold`):

| n  | p = 1/n        | C(n,3)·p³           | triangle-free w.p. > 0? |
|----|----------------|---------------------|--------------------------|
| 10 | 0.1            | 120·0.001 = 0.120   | yes                      |
| 20 | 0.05           | 1140·1.25e-4 ≈ 0.143| yes                      |
| 50 | 0.02           | 19600·8e-6 ≈ 0.157  | yes                      |

In every row `C(n,3)·p³ < 1`, so `triangle_threshold` yields a positive
probability of triangle-freeness, consistent with the classical `p = n^{-1}`
threshold.

## 5. Counterexample hunt

- Tried to drop `0 ≤ p ≤ 1` from the probabilistic inequalities: fails, because
  `weight` can be negative (e.g. `p = 2` makes `1 - p < 0`), breaking
  `Finset.sum_nonneg`. Hypotheses kept.
- Tried to drop nonnegativity of `X` from `second_moment_core`: **no
  counterexample** — the identity `X·𝟙_{X≠0} = X` holds for all real `X`, so the
  bound `P(X=0)·𝔼[X]² ≤ Var(X)` is in fact valid unconditionally. The hypothesis
  was removed, strengthening the lemma.

# Future Directions — Erdős–Rényi Threshold Phenomena

Derived from the cycle that produced `Model.lean`, `SecondMoment.lean`, and
`SubgraphCounting.lean`.  Each conjecture is bold, falsifiable, and stated so it
can be attacked directly in the present finite model.

## C1. Matching lower threshold for triangles (second-moment direction)

**Conjecture.** In the finite `G(n,p)` model, if `n³ p³ → ∞` then
`P(triangleCount = 0) → 0`; concretely, `Var(triangleCount) / 𝔼[triangleCount]²
→ 0`, so `second_moment` forces a.a.s. existence of a triangle. Together with the
proven `triangle_threshold` this establishes the sharp threshold `p = n^{-1}`.

The key insight is that `Var(triangleCount)` is dominated by *edge-sharing pairs*
of triangles, whose count is `Θ(n⁴)`, so `Var/𝔼² = Θ(n⁴ p⁵)/Θ(n⁶ p⁶) = Θ(1/(n²p))
→ 0` exactly when `n²p → ∞` — strictly weaker than the `n³p³ → ∞` needed for the
mean to blow up, which is why the second moment method is tight here.

Why now? The division-free core `second_moment_core` is already proven for
arbitrary real variables, and `expect_prod_indicator` computes the pairwise
triangle correlations directly; only the covariance bookkeeping remains.

## C2. General clique thresholds via the balance condition

**Conjecture.** For the complete graph `K_r`, the expected number of `K_r`-copies
in `G(n,p)` is `C(n,r)·p^{C(r,2)}`, and the appearance threshold is
`p = n^{-2/(r-1)}` (the value where this expectation passes through a constant).

The key insight is that the exponent `-2/(r-1)` is exactly `-v(H)/e(H)` for the
*balanced* graph `H = K_r`, so the clique thresholds are a one-parameter family
governed solely by the density `e(H)/v(H)`.

Why now? `expect_triangle_term`/`expect_triangleCount` already realize the `r = 3`
case; the same indicator-product-over-a-fixed-edge-set computation generalizes
verbatim once the `C(r,2)`-element edge set of a clique is built.

## C3. Connectivity threshold via isolated vertices

**Conjecture.** In `G(n,p)` the expected number of isolated vertices is
`n·(1-p)^{n-1}`, and the connectivity threshold `p = ln n / n` is precisely the
point where this expectation passes through a constant; below it, isolated
vertices (hence disconnection) appear a.a.s.

The key insight is that disconnection at the threshold is *driven entirely by
isolated vertices* — the dominant obstruction — so a first/second moment analysis
of the single statistic "number of degree-0 vertices" already locates the sharp
threshold `ln n / n`.

Why now? Isolated-vertex count is a sum of per-vertex indicators whose
expectation is an immediate `expect_prod` instance (`(1-p)^{n-1}` per vertex),
making it the most accessible of the classical thresholds in this framework.

## C4. Exact second moment / variance formula for subgraph counts

**Conjecture.** For any fixed graph `H`, `Var(X_H)` in `G(n,p)` admits a closed
form as a finite sum over the ways two copies of `H` can overlap, each term a
monomial `C·p^{2e(H) - e(overlap)}`.

The key insight is that `𝔼[X_H²] = ∑_{H₁,H₂} p^{|E(H₁) ∪ E(H₂)|}` factorizes by
the size of the shared edge set, turning variance into pure edge-set combinatorics
— no probability beyond `expect_prod_indicator`.

Why now? `expect_prod_indicator` already gives `𝔼[∏_{e∈S} 𝟙] = p^{|S|}` for an
arbitrary edge set `S`, which is exactly the per-overlap term; assembling the
variance is a finite double sum.

## C5. Poisson limit at the exact threshold window

**Conjecture.** At `p` chosen so that `𝔼[triangleCount] → λ > 0`, the factorial
moments satisfy `𝔼[(triangleCount)_k] → λ^k`, the signature of a Poisson(λ) limit;
hence `P(triangleCount = 0) → e^{-λ}`.

The key insight is that distinct triangles are *asymptotically independent* in the
critical window, so the `k`-th factorial moment collapses to `λ^k` because
edge-sharing configurations are lower order.

Why now? The factorial moments are sums of `expect_prod_indicator` values over
ordered `k`-tuples of triangles, so the entire statement reduces to counting
edge-disjoint vs. edge-sharing tuples — a refinement of the C4 bookkeeping.
